coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Historic Building 12
record.summary: The 1941 Navy-built plate shop and mold loft at the heart of the World War II 'New Yard' (248 ft square, Aiken monitor roof), the first and so far only Phase 1 building delivered under Brookfield's Pier 70 DDA: lifted about ten feet against sea-level rise, rebuilt by Perkins&Will and Plant Construction as a ground-floor market hall, second-floor maker studios and third-floor offices, and issued a temporary certificate of occupancy in January 2022. Held on a 66-year, $1-a-year Port lease; nearly 90% leased by August 2026, with General Catalyst taking the whole third floor.

facts.value: 1070 Maryland St (Brookfield's Building 12 page; the 2023 Real Deal report gives 180 Maryland Street)

248 ft 2 in by 242 ft 2 in by 59 ft 6 in tall; Aiken roof with five glazed monitors

118,890 over two floors historically (NRHP); 230,000 sq ft after adaptive reuse per the architect (contractor: 220,000 sq ft, 60,000 sq ft main warehouse plus a 45,000 sq ft mezzanine and 60,000 sq ft of office); about 200,000 sq ft per the 2026 Real Deal report
Ground-floor market hall with large-scale production and retail, second-floor maker and artisan studios, third-floor office
Structure raised approximately 10 feet (architect) / 12 feet (ENR, contractor) to sit above 100-year sea-level-rise projections; the Port's 2018 release said 9 feet
66 years from the Port at $1/year base rent with participation rent from year 31 (DDA terms)

Standard Deviant Brewing, Breadbelly, Sven Ceramics, Bay Padel, The Plenary Co., Studio Duskus, Marbled Mint, Prowl Studio, Scuderia, Zai Divecha and Emi Grannis; two venture capital firms on the third floor (General Catalyst and Monograph Capital)
ENR California Best Projects Award of Merit 2022; AIA California Honor Award 2024; AIA San Francisco Honor Award for adaptive reuse 2024; WAN Silver 2023 (architect's list)
Plate shop and mold loft for hull construction at Slips 5-8; vacant at the time of the 2013 nomination

changes.text: The owner flagged that Standard Deviant Brewing, open at 1070 Maryland St (Building 12) since its June 6, 2025 grand opening, was missing. Confirmed via press coverage; it never surfaced in the DataSF registration join at all (checked out/retail_candidates.csv and the raw business-locations pull directly) because it has no Registered Business Location record under any name at that address as of the 2026-09-22 data pull -- a real gap in DataSF's own dataset, not a join bug like the earlier approximate-geometry drops. open_questions: Construction cost of the Building 12 rehabilitation itself: not stated anywhere; only the $237.4M Phase 1 total (Oct 2022) and the $150M infrastructure Notice of Completion figure exist.
Whether the 66-year Building 12 lease has been executed, and its date: the DDA sets the trigger, but no Port Commission lease approval for Building 12 was found on 2018-2026 agendas.
The lift height is given as 9 ft (Port, 2018), 10 ft (Perkins&Will) and 12 ft (ENR, Plant); square footage as 200,000-230,000 depending on source.
The address appears as 1070 Maryland Street (Brookfield, 2026 reports) and 180 Maryland Street (2023 Real Deal report); status.csv uses 1070.
No 'now' photograph with a stated license was found; the D4D images hosted here pre-date the rehabilitation.

The four D4D-credited photographs of Building 12 (building12.jpg, building12_corrugated.jpg, building12_interior.jpg, building12_roof.jpg) are straight architectural photographs taken in 2017, not scanned drawings or plans; `kind: document` fits the schema's 'page from a source document' reading but they may read better as `before` (pre-rehabilitation condition) if the record's kind taxonomy is revisited.

record.notes: Historic Building 12, 1070 Maryland St -- ground floor plan (Building 12 leasing brochure, pier70sf.com) shows it bounded by Louisiana St (west), Maryland St (east), 22nd St (south), and Potrero Point Plaza (north); seismic retrofit/adaptive reuse complete, hosting events, and 2026 VC office lease (General Catalyst, 70,000 sqft, 3rd floor). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: previously joined to blklot 4045017 (700 Illinois St) -- that parcel is actually an unrelated residential condo building over 500m further north/west (confirmed by a user-supplied screenshot showing this project's Elevation Sky Park box, anchored on the old position, sitting on top of the real Crane Cove Park; satellite imagery then showed the old Building-12 point in an ordinary residential block, and the correct blklot 4114010 exactly outlines the real sawtooth-roofed industrial building visible in satellite imagery at 1070 Maryland St). An earlier version of this row also credited the RH showroom to this building -- that's actually Building 101, the separate 1917 Bethlehem Steel administrative building at the corner of 20th/Illinois St, ~500m away (sfchronicle.com/sf/article/pier-70-building-12-19513305.php, therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2026/01/27/vc-firm-joins-pier-70-in-significant-office-lease, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Building_101_(San_Francisco), pier70sf.com/leasing/building-12/, pier70sf.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Building-12_Digital.pdf)
